claim: Humans with certain genetic polymorphisms at the kinase suppressor of ras2 (KSR2) locus develop severe early-onset obesity and type 2 diabetes.
source: Humans with certain genetic polymorphisms at the kinase suppressor of ras2 (KSR2) locus develop severe early-onset obesity and type 2 diabetes.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature about KSR2 genetic polymorphisms in humans.

claim: Mice with Ksr2 deleted phenocopy severe early-onset obesity and type 2 diabetes observed in humans with KSR2 polymorphisms.
source: Both conditions are phenocopied in mice with Ksr2 deleted, but whether this affects bone health remains unknown.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature and the experimental design of the current study.

claim: Ksr2 negatively regulates femoral bone mass in two genetic backgrounds.
source: Here we studied the bones of global Ksr2 null mice and found that Ksr2 negatively regulates femoral, but not vertebral, bone mass in two genetic backgrounds, while the paralogous gene, Ksr1, was dispensable for bone homeostasis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from microCT analysis in two different genetic backgrounds (C57BL/6J-Tyrc-Brd × 129SvEvBrd hybrid and DBA/1LacJ).

claim: Ksr2 does not regulate vertebral bone mass.
source: Here we studied the bones of global Ksr2 null mice and found that Ksr2 negatively regulates femoral, but not vertebral, bone mass in two genetic backgrounds, while the paralogous gene, Ksr1, was dispensable for bone homeostasis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing no changes in vertebral trabecular bone parameters.

claim: Ksr1 is dispensable for bone homeostasis.
source: Here we studied the bones of global Ksr2 null mice and found that Ksr2 negatively regulates femoral, but not vertebral, bone mass in two genetic backgrounds, while the paralogous gene, Ksr1, was dispensable for bone homeostasis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing no significant differences in trabecular bone parameters between Ksr1 KO and WT mice.

claim: KSR2 regulates bone formation by influencing adipocyte differentiation at the expense of osteoblasts in the bone marrow.
source: Mechanistically, KSR2 regulates bone formation by influencing adipocyte differentiation at the expense of osteoblasts in the bone marrow.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing reduced marrow adipose tissue and increased osteoblast markers in Ksr2 KO mice.

claim: Ksr2 can regulate bone formation autonomously.
source: Compared with Ksr2's known role as a regulator of feeding by its function in the hypothalamus, pair-feeding and osteoblast-specific conditional deletion of Ksr2 reveals that Ksr2 can regulate bone formation autonomously.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from pair-feeding studies and osteoblast-specific conditional knockout experiments.

claim: Despite gains in appendicular bone mass, bone strength remains compromised in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: Despite the gains in appendicular bone mass observed in the absence of Ksr2, bone strength, as well as fracture healing response, remains compromised in these mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from three-point bending tests showing reduced load to fracture and reduced stiffness.

claim: Fracture healing response remains compromised in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: Despite the gains in appendicular bone mass observed in the absence of Ksr2, bone strength, as well as fracture healing response, remains compromised in these mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from fracture healing studies showing delayed endochondral ossification.

claim: Obesity is associated with an increased propensity for bone fractures.
source: Pathological obesity and its complications are associated with an increased propensity for bone fractures.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on obesity and bone health.

claim: Obesity afflicts nearly 40% of adults in the United States.
source: Obesity is a major public health problem in the United States, afflicting nearly 40% of adults, and has become a prevalent and destructive health disorder linked to some of the major metabolic diseases, including cardiovascular diseases, type 2 diabetes (T2D), and cancer (Devlin and Rosen, 2015; Pagnotti et al., 2019; Shanbhogue et al., 2016; Walsh and Vilaca, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on obesity prevalence.

claim: Obesity is linked to cardiovascular diseases, type 2 diabetes, and cancer.
source: Obesity is a major public health problem in the United States, afflicting nearly 40% of adults, and has become a prevalent and destructive health disorder linked to some of the major metabolic diseases, including cardiovascular diseases, type 2 diabetes (T2D), and cancer (Devlin and Rosen, 2015; Pagnotti et al., 2019; Shanbhogue et al., 2016; Walsh and Vilaca, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on obesity-related diseases.

claim: Increased body weight is associated with higher bone mineral density.
source: Although obesity may be considered beneficial to bone health, since increased body weight is associated with higher bone mineral density (BMD), the relationship between excess body fat and bone health is complex, given that obesity has been identified as a risk factor for certain fractures (Greco et al., 2015; Ma et al., 2018; Veldhuis-Vlug and Rosen, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on body weight and BMD.

claim: Obesity has been identified as a risk factor for certain fractures.
source: Although obesity may be considered beneficial to bone health, since increased body weight is associated with higher bone mineral density (BMD), the relationship between excess body fat and bone health is complex, given that obesity has been identified as a risk factor for certain fractures (Greco et al., 2015; Ma et al., 2018; Veldhuis-Vlug and Rosen, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on obesity and fracture risk.

claim: Most diet-induced obesity studies have reported reduced BMD and trabecular bone mass.
source: Most diet-induced obesity studies have reported reduced BMD and trabecular bone mass (Bonnet et al., 2014; Doucette et al., 2015; Inzana et al., 2013; Scheller et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on diet-induced obesity models.

claim: Monogenetic models of obesity have provided a broader range of bone phenotypes, including no change, loss, or gain in bone mass or BMD.
source: By contrast, monogenetic models of obesity have provided a broader range of bone phenotypes, including no change, loss, or gain in bone mass or BMD (Ahn et al., 2006; Baldock et al., 2007; Braun et al., 2012; Steppan et al., 2000; Wang et al., 2007a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on monogenetic obesity models.

claim: KSR1 and KSR2 were identified as mediators of energy consumption, utilization, and adipogenic regulation.
source: Recently, the scaffold proteins kinase suppressor of ras (KSR1 and KSR2) were identified as mediators of energy consumption, utilization, and adipogenic regulation (Brommage et al., 2008; Costanzo-Garvey et al., 2009; Kortum et al., 2005; Pearce et al., 2013; Revelli et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on KSR proteins.

claim: Only Ksr2 knockout mice become obese and diabetic, not Ksr1 knockout mice.
source: Although these two genes function as paralogs, we previously found that only Ksr2 knockout (KO) mice become obese and diabetic (Brommage et al., 2008; Costanzo-Garvey et al., 2009; Kortum et al., 2005; Pearce et al., 2013; Revelli et al., 2011), suggesting that these paralogs have non-redundant roles, although Ksr1 does have a role in adipogenesis (Kortum et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on Ksr1 and Ksr2 knockout mice.

claim: Several mutations at the KSR2 loci in humans have been associated with severe early-onset obesity.
source: Several mutations at the KSR2 loci in humans have been associated with severe early-onset obesity (Pearce et al., 2013), and studies in Ksr2 KO mice have revealed a centrally regulated mechanism by Ksr2 expression and function in the hypothalamus that results in hyperphagia, changes in metabolic rate, and consequently, obesity and T2D (Costanzo-Garvey et al., 2009; Guo et al., 2017; Henry et al., 2014; Pearce et al., 2013; Revelli et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on KSR2 mutations in humans.

claim: Ksr2 expression and function in the hypothalamus results in hyperphagia, changes in metabolic rate, and consequently, obesity and T2D.
source: Several mutations at the KSR2 loci in humans have been associated with severe early-onset obesity (Pearce et al., 2013), and studies in Ksr2 KO mice have revealed a centrally regulated mechanism by Ksr2 expression and function in the hypothalamus that results in hyperphagia, changes in metabolic rate, and consequently, obesity and T2D (Costanzo-Garvey et al., 2009; Guo et al., 2017; Henry et al., 2014; Pearce et al., 2013; Revelli et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on Ksr2 function in the hypothalamus.

claim: Ksr2 gene deletion is associated with a profound obese phenotype and lethality at a young age.
source: Although there are hundreds of mouse genes reported to lead to obesity when disrupted, Ksr2 gene deletion is associated with a profound obese phenotype and lethality at a young age (Brommage et al., 2008; Revelli et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on Ksr2 knockout mice.

claim: Loss of KSR2 function increases long bone trabecular bone mass.
source: Our studies show that loss of KSR2 function increases long bone trabecular bone mass while reducing marrow adiposity and that KSR2 acts as a molecular switch that controls the differentiation of bone resident mesenchymal stem cells into osteoblast or adipocyte differentiation via an mTOR-dependent mechanism.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from microCT analysis showing increased trabecular bone parameters in Ksr2 KO mice.

claim: Loss of KSR2 function reduces marrow adiposity.
source: Our studies show that loss of KSR2 function increases long bone trabecular bone mass while reducing marrow adiposity and that KSR2 acts as a molecular switch that controls the differentiation of bone resident mesenchymal stem cells into osteoblast or adipocyte differentiation via an mTOR-dependent mechanism.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from osmium tetroxide microCT and histological analysis showing reduced marrow adipose tissue in Ksr2 KO mice.

claim: KSR2 acts as a molecular switch that controls the differentiation of bone resident mesenchymal stem cells into osteoblast or adipocyte differentiation via an mTOR-dependent mechanism.
source: Our studies show that loss of KSR2 function increases long bone trabecular bone mass while reducing marrow adiposity and that KSR2 acts as a molecular switch that controls the differentiation of bone resident mesenchymal stem cells into osteoblast or adipocyte differentiation via an mTOR-dependent mechanism.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from in vitro studies showing KSR2 regulates osteoblast differentiation through mTOR signaling.

claim: Distal femoral metaphyseal bones of Ksr2 KO female mice exhibited increased trabecular bone mass at both 11 and 15 weeks of age.
source: Distal femoral metaphyseal bones of Ksr2 KO (Ksr2-/-) female mice exhibited increased trabecular bone mass at both 11 and 15 weeks of age (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by microCT data and images showing increased trabecular bone in Ksr2 KO mice.

claim: By 11 weeks, bone volume fraction (BV/TV) and trabecular thickness (Tb.Th) were significantly increased in female Ksr2 KO mice.
source: Quantification of trabecular parameters at the distal femur secondary spongiosa shows that by 11 weeks bone volume fraction (BV/TV), and trabecular thickness (Tb.Th) were significantly increased in female KO mice (Figure 1C and G)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative microCT data shown in Figure 1C and G.

claim: Structure model index (SMI) was significantly reduced in female Ksr2 KO mice at 11 weeks.
source: while structure model index (SMI), a measure of rod to plate-like trabecular morphology (Hildebrand and Rüegsegger, 1997), was significantly reduced (Figure 1E)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative microCT data shown in Figure 1E and citation to the definition of SMI.

claim: Structural morphological changes elicited by the absence of Ksr2 promote gains in bone mass.
source: overall implying that structural morphological changes elicited by the absence of Ksr2 promote gains in bone mass.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined microCT data showing increased BV/TV, Tb.Th, and reduced SMI.

claim: Mean trabecular connectivity density (CONN.D) and trabecular number (Tb.N) were increased in Ksr2 KO mice at 11 weeks, but not significantly until 15 weeks.
source: Although mean trabecular connectivity density (CONN.D) and trabecular number (Tb.N) were also increased in KO mice at 11 weeks (Figure 1D and F), these differences were not significant until 15 weeks, as was the reduction in trabecular spacing (Figure 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative microCT data shown in Figures 1D, F, and H.

claim: Trabecular bone parameters at the primary spongiosa showed significant increases in trabecular bone volume in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: To determine whether new bone formation at the primary spongiosa is altered in the Ksr2 KO mice, we measured trabecular bone parameters at the primary spongiosa, limited to within 300 μm of the distal-most femoral metaphyseal bone from the growth plate (Figure 1I–M) and found significant increases in trabecular bone volume.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative microCT data shown in Figure 1I-M.

claim: Ksr2 deleted males exhibited significantly greater BV/TV, Conn. Den, Tb.N, and Tb.Th but reduced Tb.Sp and SMI compared to littermate control mice.
source: Ksr2 deleted males also exhibited significantly greater BV/TV, Conn. Den, Tb.N, and Tb.Th but reduced Tb.Sp and SMI compared to littermate control mice (Figure 2A–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative microCT data shown in Figure 2A-G.

claim: Loss of the Ksr2 gene promotes trabecular bone density in both genders of mice.
source: Thus, loss of the Ksr2 gene promotes trabecular bone density in both genders of mice.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined data showing increased trabecular bone parameters in both female and male Ksr2 KO mice.

claim: Total tissue volume, indicative of bone size, remained unchanged in the Ksr2 KO mice in both genders.
source: While total tissue volume, indicative of bone size, remained unchanged in the KO mice in both genders (Figures 1N–P–2H–K), a significant increase in bone volume fraction was observed, although gains in BMD were more prominent in females.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative microCT data shown in Figures 1N-P and 2H-K.

claim: A significant increase in bone volume fraction was observed in mid-shaft femoral cortical bones of Ksr2 KO mice.
source: While total tissue volume, indicative of bone size, remained unchanged in the KO mice in both genders (Figures 1N–P–2H–K), a significant increase in bone volume fraction was observed, although gains in BMD were more prominent in females.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative microCT data shown in Figures 1N-P and 2H-K.

claim: Gains in BMD in mid-shaft femoral cortical bones were more prominent in females than males.
source: While total tissue volume, indicative of bone size, remained unchanged in the KO mice in both genders (Figures 1N–P–2H–K), a significant increase in bone volume fraction was observed, although gains in BMD were more prominent in females.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative microCT data shown in Figures 1N-P and 2H-K.

claim: Obese Ksr2 null mice present increased gains in trabecular and cortical mass of femoral bones.
source: Nonetheless, this evaluation reveals that obese Ksr2 null mice present increased gains in trabecular and cortical mass of femoral bones.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined microCT data showing increased trabecular and cortical bone parameters in Ksr2 KO mice.

claim: Trabecular bone measurements were nearly identical between Ksr1 KO and WT mice, irrespective of gender.
source: In contrast with the striking differences found in trabecular bone parameters in Ksr2 KO mice at this age, trabecular bone measurements were nearly identical between Ksr1 KO and WT mice, irrespective of gender (Figure 2L and M).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative microCT data shown in Figure 2L-Q.

claim: The KSR1 protein is highly unlikely to synergize with KSR2 in regulating femoral bone growth.
source: These results suggest that the KSR1 protein is highly unlikely to synergize with KSR2 in regulating femoral bone growth.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the lack of bone phenotype in Ksr1 KO mice compared to Ksr2 KO mice.

claim: Deletion of Ksr2 exon 4 in the DBA/1LacJ strain did not significantly affect the anus to nose body length.
source: Deletion of exon 4 in this genetic background did not significantly affect the anus to nose body length, although a substantial gain in body weight and percent body fat was observed by 8 weeks of age (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Deletion of Ksr2 exon 4 in the DBA/1LacJ strain resulted in substantial gain in body weight and percent body fat by 8 weeks of age.
source: Deletion of exon 4 in this genetic background did not significantly affect the anus to nose body length, although a substantial gain in body weight and percent body fat was observed by 8 weeks of age (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: DXA measurements revealed substantial increases in total body BMD in Ksr2 KO mice in the DBA/1LacJ background.
source: Concordant with Ksr2 deletion in the C57BL/6J-Tyrc-Brd × 129SvEvBrd hybrid background, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) measurements of pooled genders revealed substantial increases in total body BMD (Figure 3E)
evidence: This claim is supported by DXA data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: DXA measurements revealed substantial increases in femoral BMD in Ksr2 KO mice in the DBA/1LacJ background.
source: and, in particular, in femoral BMD (Figure 3G), while femur length remained unchanged relative to WT siblings (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by DXA data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Femur length remained unchanged in Ksr2 KO mice in the DBA/1LacJ background relative to WT siblings.
source: and, in particular, in femoral BMD (Figure 3G), while femur length remained unchanged relative to WT siblings (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by DXA data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: No changes were observed in the vertebral trabecular bone in Ksr2 KO mice in the DBA/1LacJ background.
source: Additionally, no changes were observed in the vertebral trabecular bone (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by microCT data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Histological evaluation revealed increased amounts of calcified bone in Ksr2 KO mice as the ratio of bone area over total area was increased.
source: Histological evaluation of longitudinal distal metaphyseal femur bone sections by alizarin red also revealed increased amounts of calcified bone in Ksr2 KO mice as the ratio of bone area over total area was increased, while osteoid area over bone area was decreased (Figure 3H–J, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 3H-J.

claim: Osteoid area over bone area was decreased in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: Histological evaluation of longitudinal distal metaphyseal femur bone sections by alizarin red also revealed increased amounts of calcified bone in Ksr2 KO mice as the ratio of bone area over total area was increased, while osteoid area over bone area was decreased (Figure 3H–J, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 3H-J.

claim: Qualitative comparisons suggest an increased areal expansion of IBSP and SPP1 throughout the metaphysis in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: Moreover, qualitative comparisons of bone markers, integrin bone sialoprotein (IBSP) and secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1), by immunofluorescence suggest an increased areal expansion of both markers throughout the metaphysis in KO mice (Figure 3Q and R).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence images shown in Figure 3Q-R.

claim: Ksr2 negatively regulates appendicular bone formation, with confirmation in a different genetic background.
source: Overall, this data provides further supporting evidence that Ksr2 negatively regulates appendicular bone formation, with confirmation in a different genetic background.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined data showing increased bone formation in Ksr2 KO mice in two different genetic backgrounds.

claim: Histomorphometric analysis resulted in increased calcein labeling in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: To determine whether increased bone formation is the cause of increased bone mass in Ksr2 KO mice, we performed histomorphometric analysis by pulsed calcein injections in 8-week-old mice. This resulted in increased calcein labeling in KO mice, with quantitative gains detected in bone formation rate and mineral apposition rate (Figure 3K–M).
evidence: This claim is supported by histomorphometric data shown in Figure 3K-M.

claim: Quantitative gains in bone formation rate and mineral apposition rate were detected in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: This resulted in increased calcein labeling in KO mice, with quantitative gains detected in bone formation rate and mineral apposition rate (Figure 3K–M).
evidence: This claim is supported by histomorphometric data shown in Figure 3K-M.

claim: The percentage of bone-resorbing ACP5+ osteoclasts scored per bone surface did not change in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: By contrast, the percentage of bone-resorbing acid phosphatase 5, tartrate-resistant (ACP5+) osteoclasts scored per bone surface, did not change (Figure 3N).
evidence: This claim is supported by histomorphometric data shown in Figure 3N.

claim: Serum levels of P1NP were elevated in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: Moreover, serum levels of osteoblast bone deposition (procollagen type 1 N-terminal propeptide [P1NP]) were elevated in KO mice, while those of osteoclast activity (carboxy-terminal cross-linked telopeptide of type 1 collagen [CTX1]) were not changed (Figure 3O and P).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3O.

claim: Serum levels of CTX1 were not changed in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: Moreover, serum levels of osteoblast bone deposition (procollagen type 1 N-terminal propeptide [P1NP]) were elevated in KO mice, while those of osteoclast activity (carboxy-terminal cross-linked telopeptide of type 1 collagen [CTX1]) were not changed (Figure 3O and P).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3P.

claim: mRNA expression levels of Spp1 and Sp7 were significantly increased in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: mRNA expression levels of osteoblast markers, Alpl and Bglap2, showed increased, though insignificant, expression in KO mice, while Spp1 and Sp7 were significantly increased.
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3S.

claim: Markers of differentiated osteoclasts, Acp5 and Ctsk, remained unchanged in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: By contrast, markers of differentiated osteoclasts, Acp5 and Ctsk, remained unchanged (Figure 3S).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3S.

claim: Ksr2 affects osteoblast function, and does not apparently affect osteoclasts.
source: Combined, these results posit that Ksr2 affects osteoblast function, and does not apparently affect osteoclasts.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined data showing increased osteoblast markers and activity but no changes in osteoclast markers and activity.

claim: Ksr2 KO mice exhibit increased visceral and subcutaneous adiposity.
source: As Ksr2 KO mice are obese, exhibiting increased visceral and subcutaneous adiposity (Figure 4A)
evidence: This claim is supported by visual observation shown in Figure 4A.

claim: mRNA levels of Pparg and Cebpa were unchanged in both white and brown fat depots in Ksr2 KO mice at 28 weeks of age.
source: we determined whether genetic disruption of Ksr2 influences adipocyte gene expression in white and brown adipose tissues in 28-week-old mice. mRNA levels of key transcription factors, Pparg and Cebpa, were unchanged in both fat depots in Ksr2 KO mice (Figure 4B) at this age.
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The adipokine leptin (Lep) was increased in both white and brown fat of Ksr2 KO mice.
source: By contrast, the adipokine leptin (Lep) was increased, while complement factor D (Cfd) was decreased in both white and brown fat of Ksr2 KO mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Complement factor D (Cfd) was decreased in both white and brown fat of Ksr2 KO mice.
source: By contrast, the adipokine leptin (Lep) was increased, while complement factor D (Cfd) was decreased in both white and brown fat of Ksr2 KO mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: KSR2 exerts opposite effects on leptin and complement factor D/adipsin expression in fat tissues.
source: This suggests that KSR2 exerts opposite effects on leptin and complement factor D/adipsin expression in fat tissues, which is consistent with changes observed in other models of obesity in mice (Cianflone et al., 2003; Kwon et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the RT-qPCR data and supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Marrow adipose tissue (MAT) volume is inversely correlated with trabecular bone mass.
source: Bone marrow stem/stromal cells (BMSCs) represent common precursors for adipocytes and osteoblasts, and marrow adipose tissue (MAT) volume is known to be inversely correlated with trabecular bone mass (Ko et al., 2021; Pierce et al., 2019; Tencerova et al., 2018; Yue et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on MAT and bone mass.

claim: MAT volume was significantly reduced in all three compartments (proximal and distal metaphysis, and diaphysis) in the tibia of Ksr2 KO mice compared with controls.
source: To determine whether MAT volume is affected in the Ksr2 KO mice, we evaluated the levels of osmium tetroxide retaining MAT in femurs of 28-week-old mice by microCT (Figure 4D). MAT volume was significantly reduced in all three compartments (proximal and distal metaphysis, and diaphysis) in the tibia of Ksr2 KO mice compared with controls (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by osmium tetroxide microCT data shown in Figure 4D-E.

claim: There was a significant reduction in adipocytes in the distal femoral metaphysis of Ksr2 KO mice.
source: Consistent with these data, there was a significant reduction in adipocytes in the distal femoral metaphysis of Ksr2 KO mice (Figure 4 F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 4F-G.

claim: Neither markers associated with white adipocytes (Fabp4, Slc7a10) or brown adipocytes (Ucp1, Prdm16) were different in Ksr2 KO femurs.
source: Neither markers associated with white adipocytes (Fabp4, Slc7a10) or brown adipocytes (Ucp1, Prdm16) were different in Ksr2 KO femurs, while of the adipogenic regulatory transcription factors evaluated, Pparg was mildly but significantly reduced, and Cebpa was not changed.
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Pparg was mildly but significantly reduced in Ksr2 KO femurs.
source: Neither markers associated with white adipocytes (Fabp4, Slc7a10) or brown adipocytes (Ucp1, Prdm16) were different in Ksr2 KO femurs, while of the adipogenic regulatory transcription factors evaluated, Pparg was mildly but significantly reduced, and Cebpa was not changed.
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Key adipokines (Lep, Cfd) were decreased in Ksr2 KO femurs.
source: However, key adipokines (Lep, Cfd) were decreased (Figure 4H).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Only Wnt8b was decreased, and Ccnd1 was increased in the bones of Ksr2 KO mice among Wnt-related genes evaluated.
source: Since Wnt signaling is critically involved in regulating adipocyte differentiation, we also measured mRNA levels of several Wnt-related genes, but only found a decrease in Wnt8b, and an increase in Ccnd1, a Wnt target gene, in the bones of Ksr2 KO mice (Figure 4I).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Changes in adipokine gene expression in both body and MAT adipocytes are altered when Ksr2 is deleted globally.
source: Thus, changes in adipokine gene expression in both body and MAT adipocytes are altered when Ksr2 is deleted globally.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined RT-qPCR data showing changes in adipokine expression in both body fat and bone marrow.

claim: X-ray analysis 3 weeks after fracture showed improved bony union of the callus in WT mice and increased callus size in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: Healing response was compared between WT and KO mice at 16 weeks of age following stabilized closed femoral fractures (Figure 5A). X-ray analysis 3 weeks after fracture showed improved bony union of the callus in WT mice and increased callus size in KO mice (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by X-ray images shown in Figure 5B.

claim: MicroCT measurements showed increased total volume in the fracture callus of Ksr2 KO mice.
source: MicroCT measurements also showed increased total volume in the fracture callus of KO mice (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by microCT data shown in Figure 5C-D.

claim: An increase in low-density woven bone volume was observed in Ksr2 KO fracture callus but no changes were observed in high-density cortical bone volume.
source: When the callus was segmented into low and high densities for analysis, an increase in low-density woven bone volume was observed in Ksr2 KO fracture callus but no changes were observed in high-density cortical bone volume (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by microCT data shown in Figure 5E-F.

claim: The low-density callus BV/TV in the Ksr2 KO fractures was not significantly different from WT.
source: Consequently, the low-density callus BV/TV in the Ksr2 KO fractures was not significantly different from WT, while the high-density BV/TV callus was reduced in Ksr2 KO mice (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by microCT data shown in Figure 5E-F.

claim: The high-density BV/TV callus was reduced in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: Consequently, the low-density callus BV/TV in the Ksr2 KO fractures was not significantly different from WT, while the high-density BV/TV callus was reduced in Ksr2 KO mice (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by microCT data shown in Figure 5E-F.

claim: Ksr2 KO mice exhibited a larger fracture callus with increased low-density woven bone and reduced high-density cortical bone, consistent with delayed fracture callus development.
source: Therefore, KO mice exhibited a larger fracture callus with increased low-density woven bone and reduced high-density cortical bone, consistent with delayed fracture callus development.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined microCT data on fracture callus.

claim: Histological evaluation revealed increased Safranin O-stained cartilage in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: Histological evaluation also revealed increased Safranin O-stained cartilage in Ksr2 KO mice but no difference in TRAP+ osteoclasts compared to WT mice (Figure 5G–J)
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 5G-H.

claim: No difference in TRAP+ osteoclasts was observed in fracture callus between Ksr2 KO and WT mice.
source: Histological evaluation also revealed increased Safranin O-stained cartilage in Ksr2 KO mice but no difference in TRAP+ osteoclasts compared to WT mice (Figure 5G–J)
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 5I-J.

claim: The differences observed between WT and KO in fracture healing were not caused by differences in bone resorption, but rather by delayed endochondral ossification.
source: suggesting that the differences observed between WT and KO were not caused by differences in bone resorption, but rather by delayed endochondral ossification.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the histological data showing no difference in osteoclasts but increased cartilage.

claim: Proteins associated with hypertrophic chondrocytes, COL10A1 and IBSP, were increased in Ksr2 KO mice.
source: Proteins associated with hypertrophic chondrocytes, COL10A1 and IBSP (Gomez et al., 2022), were also increased in Ksr2 KO mice, while SP7 was reduced, indicating that the delay in bone formation occurred during the ossification of the hypertrophic cartilage (Figure 5K–N).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5K-N and citation to published literature.
